title: feat(spec): IAIConversationService.get / list and IAIService.listPendingActions take the caller's execution context
body:
Fixes #23158
Clause-②: yes (widening: an optional parameter on three published store-contract methods)

## What changes

The three AI store reads take the caller's execution context as an optional trailing parameter. This is the contract change that objectstack-ai/cloud#2844 Q1 ruling C names (maintainer 「同意」, cloud comment `6138290535`), in the shape triage's direction gives (`6139367236`).

| Method | FROM | TO |
|---|---|---|
| `IAIConversationService.get` | `get(conversationId)` | `get(conversationId, context?: ExecutionContext)` |
| `IAIConversationService.list` | `list(options?)` | `list(options?, context?: ExecutionContext)` |
| `IAIService.listPendingActions` | `listPendingActions?(filter?)` | `listPendingActions?(filter?, context?: ExecutionContext)` |

The TSDoc states the rule an implementation follows:
- **Supplied:** the implementation passes it unchanged as the `context` of every engine read the method makes (`BaseEngineOptions.context`), so the read runs as that caller. Under ADR-0096 D5 strict mode an engine read with no principal is refused with 403.
- **Omitted:** the read stays the one the implementation made before this parameter existed.
- `list`'s `options.userId` is called out as a filter on the owner. It is not the caller's identity.
- Whether a caller is admitted to the rows is the stored objects' access and sharing question, which these contracts do not declare.

Files: `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` (three signatures, their TSDoc, and one type-only import), a pin file beside it, and `.changeset/23158-ai-store-caller-context.md` (`@objectstack/spec` `minor`, carrying the `Clause-②` line and the FROM → TO). No generated artifact moved (`check:generated` green, see below). No object's `access` or sharing changed.

## Measurements

### H1: "the shape the other store contracts use"

Population at `origin/main` `de24373ec`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/*.ts` (test files excluded): the methods that take the caller's context.

| Spelling | Contract: methods (lines) |
|---|---|
| positional `context: ExecutionContext`, required | `sharing-service.ts`: 15 (`:249`–`:588`) · `approval-service.ts`: 12 (`:881`–`:996`) · `share-link-service.ts`: 3 (`:237`, `:245`, `:256`) |
| positional `context?: ExecutionContext`, optional | `analytics-service.ts`: 3 (`:312`, `:329`, `:351`) |
| positional `context?: SecurityContext` (a `Partial` of `ExecutionContext`) | `security-service.ts`: 20 (`:418`–`:1049`) |
| a field in an options bag | `data-engine.ts` `options?: BaseEngineOptions` (`:289`–`:311`) · `objectql-engine.ts:198` · `knowledge-service.ts:43` (`executionContext?`) · `automation-service.ts:709` |

The majority is `ExecutionContext` from `../kernel/execution-context.zod.js`, as a positional parameter after the method's own arguments: 33 methods across 4 contracts. In 31 of the 33 it is the last parameter, and in the other 2 one optional bag follows it. `approval-service.ts`'s `listRequests(filter, context)` has the same shape as `list` here. The parameter is optional, as triage directs and as `IAnalyticsService` already does. The import specifier carries `.js`, as 5 of the 7 sibling imports do.

**Conflict, stated rather than resolved silently:** the card body's ask said "the same shape the engine's read verbs take", which is the options-bag form. Triage's direction (Zone 1, binding) says "the shape the other store contracts use", and this PR follows triage. The two forms meet at the engine call: the type-level pin below proves `ExecutionContext` is assignable to `BaseEngineOptions['context']`, so an implementation forwards it with no conversion.

### H2: where the objects live, and the owner-reads-own-rows reading: NOT MEASURED here

None of the four objects is declared in this repository. On `origin/main` `de24373ec`, a `git grep` for the declaration spelling `name: 'OBJECT'` returns nothing for `ai_conversations`, `ai_messages`, `ai_pending_actions` or `ai_agent_memories`. The only hits are test fixtures in `plugin-sharing` and name references in the share-link routes. The control leg is the same grep for `name: 'sys_user'`, which hits `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts:46`. This repository's liveness ledger (`packages/spec/liveness/agent.json:96`) cites the store at `cloud @ef5a4344: packages/service-ai/src/agent-memory.ts#AgentMemoryStore — the store, over the object ai_agent_memories (access private, no API)`. I did not read that file directly.

So triage's measurement ("with a caller threaded through, does an ordinary member read their own rows on these `access: private` objects?") cannot run in this repository. It can run in objectstack-ai/cloud's `service-ai`, with this contract at cloud's pin. The cloud card that switches the 18 reads back to the caller's identity is the natural place to measure it. **No sharing card is filed on an unmeasured premise.** If that measurement shows an owner is refused, the sharing question is filed then, from there.

### H3: the pins, without an in-repo implementer

`git grep` on `origin/main` finds no implementer of `IAIConversationService` or of `IAIService.listPendingActions` in this repository. The only users are `ai-service.test.ts`'s mocks and a type reference in `packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts:67`, which never calls these methods. So the pins in `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-store-caller-context.pin.test.ts` are contract-level:
- **Type level** (compiled by `check:test-typecheck` under `tsconfig.test.json`):
  - each method's trailing parameter is exactly `ExecutionContext | undefined`, and nothing follows it (arity `1 | 2` / `0 | 1 | 2`);
  - `ExecutionContext` is assignable to the non-null `BaseEngineOptions['context']`;
  - an implementation written against the shorter signatures still satisfies each method type;
  - calls without the context compile.
- **Runtime:** a minimal in-test implementation, over a recording engine port typed as `IDataEngine`'s `find` / `findOne` (a `Pick`), is written to the TSDoc's forwarding rule.
  - With a member context, every engine read (`get` makes two, `ai_conversations` then `ai_messages`) carries it as `options.context`, by reference, and the real `BaseEngineOptionsSchema.safeParse` accepts those options.
  - Without one, each engine read gets no options argument at all, which is the call the shorter signature made.
  - The runtime half pins the rule as executable reference. It cannot pin `service-ai`, and that implementer's own conformance lives with it.

**Reverse verification (ablation), one per method, from the committed state** (the HEAD blob of `ai-service.ts` is `84b68834da23`). Each leg ran through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit 1 → 0, the blob changed, and on restore the blob equalled HEAD and `git diff HEAD` was empty. No `dist/` rebuild was needed, because the pin imports `./ai-service` and `../data/data-engine.zod` by relative path, so the program reads `src/`. Measured with the spec test-layer program (`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`):

| Leg | Pin-file errors | Program total | What went red |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (HEAD) | 0 | 246 (the ledger's 246) | none |
| `get` without `context` | 7 | 253 | `GetTakesTheCallerContext` and `GetArity` (TS2344), TS2493, the in-test `get` (TS2322 / TS7006), the two-argument call (TS2554) |
| `list` without `context` | 7 | 253 | `ListTakesTheCallerContext` and `ListArity`, the same classes |
| `listPendingActions` without `context` | 7 | 253 | `ListPendingActionsTakesTheCallerContext` and `ListPendingActionsArity`, the same classes |

The observed direction is turning red, at the type layer. The runtime half stays green under each ablation, because types are erased at run time. That is expected: the contract is a type, and the type half is what fails.

### H4: the typecheck debt ledger

The pinned entry `src/contracts/ai-service.test.ts`: `TS2739 … missing … getTurnState, update` is unmoved. A mock written against the shorter `get` / `list` stays assignable, so no new signature arrives. `check:test-typecheck` is green with the ledger untouched: `52 file(s) / 246 error(s) / 135 pinned signature(s) held`. The new pin file compiles with zero errors. `packages/spec/test-typecheck-debt.json` is not in this diff.

## Verification

Readings taken at HEAD `c128fd10a`: this branch after merging `origin/main` `32fa1942e`, which touched `packages/spec` in disjoint files.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The rebuilt `dist/contracts/index.d.ts` carries the three new signatures (`:5745`, `:6084`, `:6094`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: exit 0, `All 14 generated artifacts are up to date`. That includes `check:api-surface` and `check:export-origins` (no export added or removed) and `check:test-typecheck`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/contracts/ai-store-caller-context.pin.test.ts src/contracts/ai-service.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 27 passed (27)`.
- The full spec suite, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 662 passed (662)`, `Tests 20114 passed | 1 todo`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derived 85 commands. Each line was run with its exit code captured before any pipe.
  - 82 exited 0 on the first pass.
  - 2 exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) and went green after their prerequisites were built. `check:doc-formula-expressions` passed after `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/formula --filter=@objectstack/lint`: `22 record-scoped formula example(s) across 474 files / 1391 TS blocks judged clean`. `check:lean-entry-closure` passed after building `@objectstack/objectql`: `Admitted set held exactly (15 packages)`.
  - 1 is **NOT MEASURED**: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which needs every package's `dist/`, so a whole-workspace build. As a declared narrowing, all 19 `@objectstack/spec` CJS require entries the gate lists (`--list`) load in a fresh `node` with 0 failures. The diff adds only a type-only import, which is erased from the emitted JS.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: `85 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 84 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED`.
- ESLint, narrowed and proven: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the two changed `.ts` files reports 2 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. Both files are in the config's population (`--print-config` resolves rules for each). The config enables no type-aware linting (`eslint.config.mjs:327`–`:328`: no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's run.
- Consumers: none in this repository call the three methods (H3). The public surface widens by an optional parameter only, so no import-side test is owed here.

## Acceptance notes

- **The card body's asks 2 and 3 are not in this PR.** Ask 2 (owner reads of the four objects) and ask 3 (a non-owner refused, the owner admitted) concern the objects, which are declared in objectstack-ai/cloud. Triage's direction keeps sharing out of this card ("⛔ no sharing widened as a rider") and routes it to a card filed only after the measurement in H2. That measurement can only run where the objects are declared.
- **Other contract reads with no caller context**, noted and not filed. `IAIConversationService.getTurnState` reads the turn's `ai_messages`, and `addMessage` / `update` answer with the conversation. None of them takes a caller context. The ruling and triage name exactly three methods, so this PR changes those three. Carrier: the cloud card that switches the 18 reads back, which will see whether any of these is among the reads D5 refuses.
